native_result.query: How did urban land use affect the invasion of different types of introduced plants?
native_result.HypoA: Urban land use reduced invasion by gardening plants over unintentionally introduced ones.
native_result.HypoB: Urban land use (2009, 50 m buffer) is most strongly and robustly associated with the presence of unintentionally introduced plants (presence odds ratio ≈ 9.4 per unit of urban cover, 95% CI 4.1–21.3, p<0.001; robust to elevation, roads, climate and cropland, and consistent at 500–1000 m) — a stronger urban association than that of gardening-introduced plants (OR ≈ 1.9, 95% CI 0.9–4.0, p=0.11; the raw urban–gardening association, OR ≈ 6.2 [3.3, 11.5], is largely explained by their shared concentration in low-elevation, mild climates). Agri-forest-introduced plants show no detectable urban association (OR ≈ 1.5, 95% CI 0.3–7.2, p=0.58) and are too underpowered (21 invaded plots) to support any conclusion; the urban signal acts on whether a pathway's invaders are present at all, not on species richness within invaded plots (count IRRs ≈ 1.0), and is largely absorbed when conditioning on habitat class.
native_result.WorkflowB: Data: invaded_niche_pathways.csv (632 plots x 37 vars, no missing); pathway counts n.gard (117 nonzero, 81.6% zero), n.unint (145, 77.1% zero), n.agfo (21, 96.7% zero). MAIN MODEL (2009, 50 m urban as focal predictor): two-part (hurdle) model per pathway — (1) 'zero/presence' logistic for P(invaded plot has >=1 species of that pathway) and (2) Poisson count on nonzero plots (richness among invaded plots) — adjusting for elevation, distance to road/stream, annual temperature/rainfall/radiation, and co-scaled cropland. Reported BOTH specifications side by side: without habitat (marginal urban association) and with 10-level habitat fixed effects (ridge-penalized logit, lambda=1, due to quasi-separation; corr(hab_Urban, urban)=0.73). As requested, a full ZINB was also fitted (custom scipy MLE; log-likelihood validated to exactly reproduce statsmodels' ZeroInflatedPoisson): the zero-inflation equation coefficients are reported alongside the count equation (ZI coefs per unit urban: Gardening -4.23, Unintentional -4.38, AgriForest -5.59; count IRRs ~1.0), with the explicit caveat that the dispersion parameter diverges (alpha -> infinity, Poisson limit) so the urban effect on presence is identifiable but its split between the count mean and the excess-zero probability is not (flat likelihood ridge, very large ZI SEs) — hence the two-part model is the well-identified presentation. SCALES: the same two-part model was refit with urban.2009.500m and urban.2009.1000m (Unintentional OR 18.8 [6.1, 58.5] and 21.8 [5.8, 82.2]; Gardening 3.0 [1.1, 8.3] and 1.6 [0.5, 5.4]; AgriForest n.s.), i.e., direction/strength consistent across scales. CHANGE: net landscape change 1956->2009 (progressive - regressive, 50 m) was used as predictor, restricted to the 592/632 rows where progressive+regressive+no.changes sums to within 0.05 of 1 (filtering rule stated here, as the columns' urban-only vs urban+cropland semantics are undetermined); Unintentional presence OR 0.70 [0.56, 0.89] per SD (p=0.003), others n.s.
